source_metadata.title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of efficacy and safety of Romosozumab in postmenopausal osteoporosis
source_metadata.source_type: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials

extraction_metadata.scope_note: Primary review methods, pooled efficacy and safety findings, review-level quality assessments, conclusions, and relevant supplement context were extracted. Trial-level claims in the systematic review remain secondary reports and are not represented as if this review generated primary participant data.

atoms.canonical_statement: The review evaluated the efficacy and safety of romosozumab in postmenopausal osteoporosis, with fracture reduction as the primary objective and BMD, falls, and safety as secondary objectives.
The systematic review followed PRISMA and was prospectively registered in PROSPERO as CRD42019112196.
Only randomized controlled trials evaluating romosozumab in postmenopausal osteoporosis were eligible; observational studies, reviews, and epidemiological studies were excluded.
The authors searched MEDLINE/PubMed, Cochrane CENTRAL, ClinicalTrials.gov, and article bibliographies on 28 May 2020 without publication-status restriction.
Two independent researchers screened titles and abstracts, two authors assessed full texts, and disagreements were resolved with the corresponding author.
The extraction form captured study design, romosozumab dose and regimen, group size, fractures, BMD, and safety outcomes.
Fracture incidence was the primary efficacy outcome.
Change in bone mineral density was a secondary outcome.
Incidence of falls was a secondary outcome.
Safety outcomes included total adverse events and serious adverse events.
Two authors independently assessed trial risk of bias with Cochrane ROB-2 and generated risk-of-bias plots with Robvis.
Publication bias was assessed by funnel plot and Egger regression; Egger testing was not used for fracture outcomes because fewer than five studies contributed.

Fractures were pooled as odds ratios, adverse events as risk ratios, and BMD as pooled mean change using a fixed-effect model in RevMan 5.3; I² greater than 50% was defined as significant heterogeneity.
Evidence certainty was assessed with GRADEpro GDT; the calculated optimal information size was 1,138 participants per group.
The meta-analysis included 10 randomized trials with 6,137 participants in romosozumab groups and 5,732 participants in control groups.

population.label: 10 included RCTs: 6,137 romosozumab-group and 5,732 control-group participants

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors rated the overall risk of bias as low for all included trials and reported no concerns in randomization, deviations from intervention, missing data, outcome measurement, or selective reporting.
The funnel plot for seven BMD studies was visually asymmetrical.
Egger testing for BMD gave t=2.2788 and p=0.0716; the authors interpreted this as low publication bias.
Egger testing gave t=0.0030, p=0.9977 for total adverse events and t=2.0755, p=0.1736 for falls; the authors characterized overall publication bias as low.
The authors rated fracture-incidence evidence as High, BMD evidence as Moderate, and evidence for total and serious adverse events as Moderate in their narrative GRADE summary.
The review characterized its overall GRADE evidence quality as High.

The authors concluded that romosozumab significantly decreases fracture incidence, significantly increases BMD, and has total and serious adverse-event rates similar to control, thereby favoring its use in postmenopausal osteoporosis.
The authors stated that further randomized trials would be very unlikely to change the overall conclusion of the review.
The authors identified use of GRADEpro GDT and an overall High GRADE assessment as a strength of the review.
The datasets used or analyzed in the review are available from the corresponding author on request.
The authors declared no conflicts of interest.
